references.text: Moses uses the same image of an eagle carrying its young on its wings, describing how the Lord led Israel through the wilderness.
Describes the actual event where the Lord brought the children of Israel out of Egypt, as verse 19:4 refers back to.
Israel saw with their own eyes what the Lord did to the Egyptians at the Red Sea, a direct fulfillment of 'you have seen what I did to the Egyptians'.
Isaiah uses the eagle image for those who wait on the Lord and will receive new strength and mount up on wings like eagles.
Moses reminds the people that they themselves have seen all that the Lord did in Egypt, the same witness appeal as in Exodus 19:4.
The woman is given two great eagle wings to fly into the wilderness, an image reflecting God's protection of His people as in Exodus.
Moses asks rhetorically if any god has taken a nation out from another nation with signs and wonders, as Israel experienced in Egypt.
Both verses confirm God's saving act from Egypt, but Exodus 19:4 emphasizes personal care (the wing image) which underpins the act of liberation in Judges.
A powerful contrast where Exodus 19:4 highlights God's faithfulness in the exodus, while 1 Samuel 8:8 uses the same event to accuse the people of having forsaken this grace.
Both verses confirm God's role as leader from Egypt to possession of the land, where Amos expands the image with the wilderness journey to emphasize God's patient guidance.
An embedded cross-reference within the same book: 10:2 establishes the purpose of remembering the plagues, while 19:4 uses the memory of these acts as the basis for the covenant.
Joshua 24:5 confirms and summarizes the specific actions (the battle against Egypt and the exodus) that God refers to in Exodus 19:4.
A theological parallel within the same book: Both verses link God's identity ('I am the Lord') directly to the act of bringing the people out of Egypt.
Joshua 24:6 expands on the context of 'eagle wings' in Exodus 19:4 by describing the dangerous situation at the sea from which God rescued His people.
